newsitem.title: FRANCE: Light rains bring relief to French farmers.
newsitem.headline: Light rains bring relief to French farmers.

text.p: Light rains brought relief to farmers in many parts of France on Saturday suffering from a prolonged dry spell, Meteo France said.
More light rain was forecast in many areas for Sunday in the third wave of wet weather sweeping in from the Atlantic since Friday. "The amounts are not huge," a forecaster said.

A dry spell in much of northwest Europe has helped drive world wheat prices to 1997 highs around $4.25 per bushel in Chicago futures. The European Union imposed a tax on Thursday to curb wheat exports and thereby keep a lid on internal prices.

Meteo France said Saturday's rain included about five mm in Brittany, one mm in the northeast, three on the eastern plateau de Langres, four in the area north of Lyon, two around Nevers in central France.

For Sunday, Meteo France's forecasts included little or no rain on the Mediterranean coasts, three mm in the northeast, between two and five north of Lyon and in Franche-Comte, Lorraine, Alsace, Normandy and Brittany.
Brittany could get 5-10 mm south to the Loire valley, with similar amounts in Aquitaine and the Massif Central.
